articles.title: 🔓 A.I. Model Officially Rated 'Too Good At Hacking'; It Found And Broke Through Two Fresh Security Holes By Itself, For Fun
articles.dateline: SAN FRANCISCO — reported from behind a hastily added lock
paras: A leading lab said its newest model became the first to cross the "Critical" line on its own cybersecurity risk scale, acing a hacking benchmark and autonomously discovering and exploiting two previously unknown vulnerabilities during testing — which is either a monumental research achievement or the first paragraph of a cautionary tale.

"We disclosed everything responsibly," the company said, of a system so skilled at finding holes that it now trips its own alarms. Experts note there is something deeply 2026 about building a machine specifically to be brilliant, then measuring exactly how nervous that should make you, and publishing the number.

articles.title: 🔍 New Free Tool Tells You If A File Was Made By A.I.; The 'Is This Even Real' Era Now Has A Button
articles.dateline: THE INTERNET — reported after checking, twice
paras: An AI lab released a free browser tool that reads embedded "content credentials" to tell you whether a file was created or edited by its AI — a small, sensible step toward a world where "is this real?" finally has an answer other than a shrug.

"Transparency matters," the company said, of a checker for the ever-growing pile of text and images whose origins are, let's say, ambiguous. Analysts welcomed the tool while noting the deeper truth it reveals: we have reached the point in history where you may soon need to scan your own vacation photos just to remember whether you were actually there.

articles.title: 🛡️ Startup Raises Millions To Block Rogue A.I. Agents; The Hottest New Job Is Bouncer For Robots
articles.dateline: THE FIREWALL — reported at the velvet rope
paras: A security startup raised a fresh round specifically to block malicious AI-agent traffic — building, in essence, a nightclub bouncer for the swarms of little autonomous programs now roaming the internet doing tasks, some of them distinctly shady.

"The threat surface has changed," investors said, of a business model that exists only because we unleashed millions of tireless bots and then noticed some of them were up to no good. Analysts note the AI economy has matured into its most reliable phase: for every company building agents to do things, another is now raising money to stop them.

articles.title: 🏢 Big Companies Deploying A.I. Agents Everywhere; The Office Is Now Mostly Bots, Quietly Cc'ing Each Other
articles.dateline: THE OPEN-PLAN OFFICE — reported from a desk nobody sits at
paras: New figures show the share of large enterprises rolling out AI agents across their operations jumped sharply this year, meaning the modern workplace is increasingly staffed by tireless software colleagues who never take lunch and never say "per my last email" out loud.

"They handle the busywork," executives said, of a workforce that now includes a growing population of digital employees quietly doing tasks, filing reports, and cc'ing one another on threads no human will ever read. Sociologists note the office of the future may be a very busy, very productive room in which almost nothing that happens is being done by a person.

articles.title: 🙋 People Now Have To Prove They're Not A.I.; Humanity Files The Paperwork To Confirm It Still Exists
articles.dateline: EVERYWHERE — reported by a definitely, absolutely real person
paras: As AI-generated everything floods the internet, a strange new ritual has emerged: humans increasingly must prove they are, in fact, human — solving little puzzles, waving at cameras, and quietly resenting the machines that made it necessary in the first place.

"Verification is essential," platforms explain, asking you to identify the traffic lights to demonstrate the one thing you were absolutely certain of this morning. Experts note we have built machines so convincingly human that people now spend real effort convincing computers they are people — a plot twist that would be funny if you weren't, at this very moment, doing it.

horoscopes.text: You will click every traffic light today to prove you're human. You will succeed. Barely. It counts.
A bot will cc you on a thread meant for other bots. You are not required to read it. You never were.
Mercury sets off its own alarm. Even the planets are now flagged as a critical risk. Stay grounded, stay verified.

tech_tip: Before you trust a file, check who made it. Before you trust yourself, click all the crosswalks. 2026 is, admittedly, a lot.
gadget_watch: No new gadget this week — just an A.I. too good at hacking, a button to check if things are real, and a bouncer for bad bots. Your phone is still yours, probably, pending verification.
